description: The take plan of the natural calibration takes (population N3): every script of one split of config/audio-qc-script-pool.json spoken by one primary voice, rotating over the language's three voices, plus a deterministic donor subset spoken by a second voice for same-script, different-voice pairs (identity-swap construction, class E). scripts/audio_qc_calibration_takes.py plans, binds and validates the takes; scripts/macos_test.sh qc-takes generates them. Takes are calibration data, never a benchmark: nothing is published and no history record is written.

generation.note: vocello batch refuses --language: every item resolves its language from its own text (Auto), as the delivered default does.

familyRule: One script x voice x seed is one family, the unit of independence (config/audio-qc-qualification-policy.json statistics.familyRule); a family is deduplicated by PCM digest.

seedRule.scope: One seed per (split, language, mode, voice) batch: vocello batch --seed applies one seed to every item of a batch. It mirrors the seed-identity scheme of scripts/language_bench_evidence.py (the first 8 bytes of a SHA-256, masked to 63 bits). A new generation number draws new, independent families.

assignment.primary: The split's scripts of a language, ordered by script ID, take the language's voices in declared order (Built-in, Built-in, Voice Design) in rotation.
assignment.donorSelection: Scripts are ranked within each primary-voice group by SHA-256 of audio-qc-calibration-donor-v1|<split>|<language>|<scriptID>; donors are drawn round-robin over the groups in voice order until the count is reached, so every ordered voice pair is represented.
assignment.donorVoice: The next voice in the rotation after the script's primary voice.

calm-narrator.text: A warm, friendly narrator with a calm, measured pace.

bright-presenter.text: A bright, youthful presenter with a lively, upbeat pace.
bright-presenter.source: the contrasting brief of this policy

calibration.expectedTakeCountRule: 10 languages x (60 primary takes + 20 donor takes)

splitRule: Calibration and confirmation are disjoint by family, speaker and script (audit section 5.5 step 1): each language's two splits share no Built-in speaker and no Voice Design brief. Japanese and Korean have one native Built-in speaker each; it speaks the calibration split, and their confirmation split relies on non-native Built-in speakers beside its Voice Design voice.
